title: Functions and Relationships: Flow Diagrams, Tables, Formulae and Equations
seo_title: Grade 8 Functions and Relationships Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Determine input values, output values or rules for patterns and relationships using flow diagrams, tables, formulae and equations; determine, interpret and justify equivalence of different descriptions of the same relationship or rule presented verbally, in flow diagrams, in tables, by formulae, by equations and by graphs on a Cartesian plane.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 8 functions worksheets: flow diagrams, tables of values, finding rules and points on a line. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Test the rule on every pair.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A function gives one output (y) for each input (x).
  • Substitute each x into the rule to fill a table: y = −2x + 3, x = −1 gives y = 5.
  • To find the rule from a table: the change in y for each step of 1 in x is the coefficient of x.
  • A point lies on the line if its coordinates make the equation true.

Examples

Example

x: 0, 1, 2, 3 and y: 4, 7, 10, 13

y goes up by 3

y = 4 when x = 0

Answer: y = 3x + 4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Wrong orderFollow the arrows.
One pair onlyTest the rule on every pair.
Negative inputs−2 × (−1) = +2.

Which expression gives the value for any n?
items.e: Each value is 3 times n: 3 × 1 = 3, 3 × 2 = 6. The expression is 3n. n + 3 gives 4, 5, 6, 7.

items.q: Which expression gives the value for any n?
items.e: The value goes up by 3, so start with 3n. When n = 1, 3 × 1 = 3, but the value is 5, so add 2: 3n + 2. 3n + 5 uses the first value as the number added.

items.q: Which expression gives the value for any n?
items.e: The value goes up by 4, so start with 4n. 4 × 1 = 4 and the value is 6, so add 2: 4n + 2. Check: 4 × 3 + 2 = 14.

items.q: Which expression gives the number of sticks in Figure n?
items.e: Count: 4, 7, 10. Each figure adds 3 sticks, so start with 3n. 3 × 1 = 3 and Figure 1 has 4, so add 1: 3n + 1. 4n counts 4 sticks for every square, but squares share sticks.

items.q: Which expression gives the number of chairs for n tables in a row?
items.e: Count: 4, 6, 8. Each table adds 2 chairs, so start with 2n. 2 × 1 = 2 and 1 table has 4 chairs, so add 2: 2n + 2. 4n gives 8 chairs for 2 tables, but there are only 6.

items.q: The number of sticks is 3n + 1. What does n stand for?
items.e: n is the input: the figure number. The whole expression 3n + 1 is the number of sticks.

items.q: The number of sticks is 3n + 1. What does the 3 tell you?
items.e: The number multiplied by n is the change from one figure to the next. Each figure adds 3 sticks. Figure 1 has 3 × 1 + 1 = 4 sticks.

items.q: Which expression gives the value for any n?
items.e: The value goes up by 2, so start with 2n. 2 × 1 = 2 and the value is 9, so add 7: 2n + 7. n + 2 writes “add 2 each time” but uses n only once.

items.q: Which expression gives the value for any n?
items.e: The value goes up by 5, so start with 5n. 5 × 1 = 5 but the value is 3, so subtract 2: 5n − 2. Check: 5 × 4 − 2 = 18.

items.q: Which expression gives the number of cubes in Figure n?
items.e: Count: 6, 9, 12. Each figure adds 3 cubes, so start with 3n. 3 × 1 = 3 and Figure 1 has 6, so add 3: 3n + 3. 6n works for Figure 1 only: 6 × 2 = 12, not 9.

items.q: What is the value of 3n + 2 when n = 7?
items.e: Replace n with 7: 3 × 7 + 2 = 21 + 2 = 23. 3n means 3 × n, not 37. Multiply before you add: 27 adds first, 3 × (7 + 2).

items.q: What is the value of 5n − 4 when n = 6?
items.e: 5 × 6 − 4 = 30 − 4 = 26. 10 subtracts first: 5 × (6 − 4). 52 reads 5n as 56. 7 adds instead of multiplying: 5 + 6 − 4.

items.q: What is the value of 2n + 9 when n = 0?
items.e: 2 × 0 + 9 = 0 + 9 = 9. Any number times 0 is 0. 11 treats 2n as 2. 29 reads 2n as 20.

items.q: What is the value of 4n + 3 when n = 10?
What is the value of 6 + 2n when n = 4?
The table follows the rule 2n + 5. What is the missing value?
items.e: Use the rule on the n above the ?: 2 × 5 + 5 = 15. 11 just adds 2 to 9, but n jumps from 2 to 5. 20 is 2 × (5 + 5). 13 is the value for n = 4.

items.q: When n goes up by 1, how much does the value of 6n + 5 go up?
items.e: Each extra 1 for n adds one more 6: 6 × 1 + 5 = 11, 6 × 2 + 5 = 17. The value goes up by 6. The + 5 stays the same.

items.q: Which list gives the values of 4n − 3 for n = 1, 2, 3, 4?
Which list gives the values of 3n + 4 for n = 1, 2, 3, 4?
items.e: 3 × 1 + 4 = 7, then add 3 each time: 7, 10, 13, 16. 4, 7, 10, 13 starts at n = 0. 3, 7, 11, 15 mixes up the 3 and the 4.

items.q: Sibusiso finds 3n + 2 when n = 4. He writes 34 + 2 = 36. What mistake did he make?
c: He should add before he multiplies

A taxi charges R4 to start plus R2 for each kilometre. The trip costs R26. How far was the trip?
items.e: Work backward. Take off the start: R26 − R4 = R22. Each km is R2: 22 ÷ 2 = 11 km. 13 km forgets the R4. 15 km adds the R4 instead of subtracting.

items.q: A swimming pool charges R12 for a card plus R3,50 for each visit. How much do 10 visits cost?
items.e: 3,50 × 10 = 35. Then R35,00 + R12,00 = R47,00. R35,00 forgets the card. R155,00 adds the card every visit.

items.q: A rain barrel holds 180 ℓ. Karabo uses 12 ℓ each day. After how many days is it empty?
items.e: 180 ÷ 12 = 15 days. Check: 180 − 12 × 15 = 0. 12 is the litres used each day, not days. After 14 days, 12 ℓ is still left.

items.q: Megan has R40 and saves R20 each week. The bike costs R300. After how many weeks can she buy it?
items.e: She still needs R300 − R40 = R260. 260 ÷ 20 = 13 weeks. Check: 20 × 13 + 40 = 300. 15 weeks forgets the R40 she has. 17 adds the R40 instead of subtracting.

items.q: A cedar seedling is 30 cm tall. It grows 15 cm each year. After how many years will it be 150 cm tall?
items.e: It needs to grow 150 − 30 = 120 cm. 120 ÷ 15 = 8 years. Check: 15 × 8 + 30 = 150. 10 years forgets the 30 cm it started with.

items.q: Lungile’s family drives on the Sea-to-Sky Highway at a steady speed. Which expression gives the distance, in kilometres, after h hours?
items.e: In 1 hour they go 60 km, so the distance is 60h. Check: 60 × 1,5 = 90. 30h uses the change in the table, but the hours go up by 0,5, not 1.

items.q: Dumisani has R90 and spends R6 each week on lunch. Sarah has R20 and saves R8 each week. After how many weeks will they have the same amount?
items.e: Each week the gap of R70 shrinks by R6 + R8 = R14. 70 ÷ 14 = 5 weeks. Check: 90 − 30 = 60 and 20 + 40 = 60. 35 divides by 8 − 6, but Dumisani goes down while Sarah goes up.

items.q: A taxi fare is given by C = 2d + 3, where d is kilometres. What does the 2 represent?
items.e: The gradient is the rate of change: each extra kilometre costs R2.

items.q: A candle is 20 cm tall and burns 2 cm every hour. Which equation gives its height h after t hours?
items.e: Start at 20 and go down 2 each hour: h = 20 − 2t, a negative gradient.

items.q: A plumber charges a R40 call-out fee plus R25 per hour. Which equation gives the cost C for h hours?
items.e: R25 for each hour, plus R40 once: C = 25h + 40.

items.q: The line y = 3x − 6 crosses the x-axis at…
Which line is steepest?
items.e: Steepness depends on the size of the gradient, ignoring its sign. |−5| is the biggest: y = −5x + 1.

items.q: Which line slopes down from left to right?
items.e: A negative gradient slopes down: y = 7 − 2x has gradient −2.

items.q: Does the point (3, 11) lie on y = 4x − 1?
A line has gradient 2 and passes through (0, −4). What is its equation?
Which two lines are parallel?
items.e: Parallel lines have the same gradient: 3x in both.

items.q: Where do y = 2x + 1 and y = 7 meet?
A water tank holds 500 litres and drains at 25 litres per minute. After how many minutes is it empty?
What is the gradient of a horizontal line?
items.e: A horizontal line does not go up or down, so its gradient is 0.
